title: El Jebel Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: El Jebel wells have a 120 ft median depth; finished well costs commonly run $12,000-$21,000.
h1: El Jebel Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost
intro_html:
Buying land around El Jebel means understanding what nearby well records can—and cannot—tell you. Within 5 miles, Colorado DWR records include 2,172 permitted wells. Reported depths have a 120-foot median, while reported pump yields have a 15.0-gpm median.

Most permits identify an unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer, so results can change from one lot to the next. The records are useful for setting expectations and reviewing neighboring wells, but a driller still needs to evaluate the exact building site, access, geology, permit requirements, and septic layout.

sections.heading: El Jebel well depths reflect mixed ground
sections.html:
Among the 1,275 wells with a reported total depth, the median is 120 feet. The middle half runs from 53 to 241 feet, and the 90th percentile is 348 feet. The deepest record reaches 1,030 feet.

Depths are spread across the area: 43% are under 100 feet, 40% are between 100 and 300 feet, 15% are between 300 and 600 feet, and 1% are deeper than 600 feet. For a drilling bid, that spread matters more than the median alone. Mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground supports a typical drilling rate of $50 to $75 per foot, but a particular lot may require substantially more hole.

sections.heading: Most El Jebel wells report strong yields
sections.html:
Only 568 wells in the records report a pump yield, so the yield data is a useful local reference rather than a guarantee for an untested parcel. The reported median is 15.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half between 14.0 and 15.0 gallons per minute.

Seventy-four percent of reported wells produce more than 15 gallons per minute. Another 24% fall between 5 and 15 gallons per minute, and 2% fall between 1 and 5 gallons per minute. No reported wells are under 1 gallon per minute. Even with these favorable records, ask how a proposed well will be tested and make sure storage, pump sizing, and household demand are considered together.

sections.heading: Water levels vary across the El Jebel record
sections.html:
Static water level is reported for 164 wells. The overall median depth to water is 33 feet, with the middle half from 15 to 148 feet below the surface. That range affects casing, pump placement, trenching, and the amount of drilling needed before water is encountered.

The decade pattern does not show a simple steady decline. Median depth to water was 35 feet in the 1970s, 44 in the 1980s, 25 in the 1990s, 15 in the 2000s, 26 in the 2010s, and 68 in the 2020s. The latest group is deeper, but the measurements come from different wells and locations, so treat the pattern as a reason to check nearby records—not proof of a uniformly dropping water table.

sections.heading: Permit history shows long local drilling activity
sections.html:
El Jebel has a long permit history, with records dating to the 1950s and the newest permit issued in 2025. Permits were issued by decade as follows: 2 in the 1950s, 71 in the 1960s, 214 in the 1970s, 267 in the 1980s, 606 in the 1990s, 394 in the 2000s, 187 in the 2010s, and 129 in the 2020s.

The most common recorded use is domestic or household at 70%. Monitoring accounts for 16%, stock for 7%, and irrigation for 6%. The busiest names in these records are Shelton Drilling Corporation, with 842 wells; Collins Drilling Co, with 192; and Steve Shelton Drilling, Inc., with 151. Confirm current licensing, availability, and scope directly before selecting a contractor.

sections.heading: What a new El Jebel well can cost
sections.html:
For the local mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground, the drilling rate model is $50 to $75 per foot. At the 120-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to about $6,000 to $9,000. That is not the complete water-system price.

A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $12,000 to $21,000 at the median depth. A deeper-than-typical hole, difficult access, casing or grout requirements, power distance, or a more complicated site plan can change the bid. Ask for a written scope that separates drilling from pump equipment, trenching, electrical, testing, permitting, and any work needed to connect the well to the home.

sections.heading: Check water quality, yield, and the building site
sections.html:
Within about 10 miles of El Jebel, mapped environmental information includes 7 PFAS sampling or contamination sites and 2 historic mine features. There are 0 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites in that mapped set. These records do not establish the quality of water at a specific parcel, so plan for a baseline water test and review the location of nearby sites before closing.

Low-yield and dry-hole risk cannot be ruled out by a favorable area median, especially where permits name fractured bedrock. Confirm the intended household use, well spacing, casing and grout details, and septic setbacks. A well and septic system also need to fit the driveway, house, replacement-area, drainage, and construction-access plan.

sections.heading: Before buying or building near El Jebel
sections.html:
Start with the neighboring permits, not just the countywide summary. Look for reported depth, yield, static water level, aquifer description, construction details, and the actual distance from the proposed well site. Nearby Catherine, Basalt, Mulford, Carbondale, Snowmass, and Cattle Creek can provide context, but the closest comparable wells are usually the most useful.

Have a Colorado well professional review the permit path before you rely on a listing’s water statement. Exempt household-use wells have defined limits, and an augmentation plan may be needed in an over-appropriated basin. For a new build, coordinate the well, septic, access driveway, utilities, and house location before excavation. That planning can prevent a well site from conflicting with the rest of the lot.

There are 0 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites in that set. Test existing or new water for appropriate local concerns, and review nearby site locations before buying.
